summary: Semantic OS transport is checksum-complete, but the visible catalog, canonical-name lookup, provenance parsing, and runtime fallback authority are incomplete and must be reconciled without hand-editing the embedded graph.
decisions: Keep the Semantic OS build graph as upstream authority and the checksum-verified Markdown payload as transport.
Generate visible Pantone coverage and provenance metadata from the payload instead of hand-editing the embedded graph.
Treat runtime neutral and state ramps as typed role policy rather than pretending every derived token is a ColorKeyword.
Preserve exact Semantic OS node identity when canonical color names are ambiguous.

gate_results.evidence: 20 passed in 1.23s; the existing suite does not cover visible Pantone completeness, canonical color_name lookup, or out-of-authority runtime defaults

22 unique Pantone HEX values are embedded-only, 20 simple COY names are not manually resolvable, 3 visible categories drift from ontology, 2 local colors lack graph relations, and 27 runtime fallback HEX values are absent from the Markdown authority

risks: The worktree already contains user-owned changes in the target color modules and tests; edits must preserve them.
Changing visible-card generation can alter runtime merge counts and must be guarded by deterministic tests.
Cerulean and Marsala have legitimate same-name, different-HEX anchors and must not be silently collapsed.
next_action: Token Curator implements deterministic visible coverage, canonical-name lookup, explicit provenance, typed runtime role policy, and regression gates; then returns a schema-valid handoff with exact changed paths and command results.
